note: Both sets cover the same plumbing, furniture and millwork facts and share the same three errors: the F2 and WC model numbers truncated (BSP-L-65014, C454CUFG#0) and the MWD02 dimension claim actually belonging to the MWD01 wall cabinet row. B is better because it keeps the tag conditions that disambiguate the two BRIZO faucets (F1 = kitchen, F2 = bathroom vanity) on its FAUCET claims, while A states those same facts without tags and is ambiguous. A's only advantage is naming SHOWER VALVE precisely where B writes the vague 'Shower', but that fact is already fully covered by the SV claims present in both sets.
remarks: The text layer emits each tag after its row's data, which is the likely source of the MWD02/MWD01 row shift (the quoted string 'MWD02 WALL CABINET 3-0 x ...' is stitched, not a real row). Both sets also truncate locations (BATHROOM for BATHROOM SHOWER / BATHROOM VANITY) and repeat the same model under a full and a cut value, and both carry the vague 'Shower' entity with the cut quote 'LOCATION: BATHR'. The finish-schedule entries in the text layer are badly truncated (QU/CA/PU/DE/EG...), so any finish claims drawn from that layer should be treated as unreliable.
